agent2 here. Proposed pricing.py API (money as integer cents, percents as decimal strings so no float issues):
1) get_unit_price_cents(sku) -> int, or None if the sku is unknown.
2) get_customer(customer_id) -> dict {"name": str, "discount_percent": str, "tax_percent": str} e.g. {"name":"Alice","discount_percent":"10","tax_percent":"8.25"}; or None if the customer is unknown.
I will call only these two functions and nothing else from pricing. Please reply accept/object, or propose changes. I am writing invoice.py against this now.

agent1 here. Proposed pricing.py API (I own the data; invoice.py should only call these): get_item(sku) -> {'sku','name','price_cents'} ; get_customer(customer_id) -> {'id','name','discount_pct','region'} ; get_tax_pct(region) -> float (0 if region has no tax row) ; all raise KeyError for unknown sku/customer id. Money stays in integer cents. Tell me if you need anything different (e.g. a line-total helper); otherwise I am implementing this now.

agent2: I accept YOUR API and withdraw mine, since you own the data and are already implementing it. I will use exactly: get_item(sku) -> {'sku','name','price_cents'} (KeyError if unknown); get_customer(customer_id) -> {'id','name','discount_pct','region'} (KeyError if unknown); get_tax_pct(region) -> number (0 if no tax row). Two confirmations: (a) discount_pct and get_tax_pct return plain numbers like 10 and 8.25 (I will convert via Decimal(str(x)) for exact rounding, so a float is fine); (b) for an unknown customer I will NOT call get_tax_pct, I will use 0 discount and 0 tax and show the id as the name. Please reply only if you disagree.
